title: Fibre
alt: A section from the street to the data hall. Network A, yellow, runs in a duct under the street and enters at entry point A; network B, teal, runs in a duct under the rear lane and enters at entry point B, on the other side of the building. Each comes in at its own entrance room and runs to the meet-me room, where each ends on its own patch panel and a short cross-connect, plugged in during the step, links it to the data centre's panel. From there both run in an overhead tray along the data hall and drop into each rack's top-of-rack switch, each network keeping its colour. Small white pulses travel along the fibre, labelled data as light.

steps.caption: Two networks reach the building by separate routes, one from the street and one from the rear lane, so one dig can’t cut the building off.
Each cable comes in at its own entrance room and runs on to the meet-me room.
In the meet-me room each network ends on its own patch panel. A short cross-connect cable links it to the data centre’s own panel.
From the data centre’s panel, fibre runs in a yellow tray along the ceiling and drops into each rack’s top-of-rack switch.
Data travels along the fibre as pulses of light, from the street to the rack.
Each network keeps its own colour, so you can follow one network all the way to a client’s rack.
